learningObjective: Distinguish how MQA/GQA affect KV memory, decode compute, and quality relative to MHA.

canonicalClaims.claim: GQA reduces per-token KV cache proportionally to H/G (where G is the number of KV groups), typically 4-8x smaller than MHA, while preserving model quality better than MQA at some KV overhead.
conditions: H is divisible by G; each group of H/G query heads shares one K/V head.
nonImplications: Does not reduce total attention FLOPs.
Does not require training from scratch: uptraining from MHA to GQA works.

canonicalClaims.claim: Empirically GQA offers a favorable quality-vs-memory point between MQA and MHA and is the standard choice for large open LLMs.
conditions: Model is trained (or uptrained) with GQA end-to-end.
nonImplications: Does not imply GQA matches MHA quality in all evaluations.

misconceptions.claim: GQA reduces attention FLOPs proportional to H/G.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FLOPs per query head are unchanged; only KV storage and read bandwidth are reduced.

misconceptions.claim: Converting an MHA model to GQA requires full retraining from random init.
misconceptions.whyWrong: 'Uptraining' averages/replicates existing KV projections and finetunes briefly.

misconceptions.claim: GQA always preserves MHA quality exactly.
misconceptions.whyWrong: GQA is a compromise; small quality gaps are typical though usually small.

implementationFacts: Llama 2 70B and Llama 3 70B use GQA with 8 KV heads.
GQA is straightforward to implement: replicate/index into KV heads when computing attention per Q head.
performanceScenarios: GQA is the main enabler of longer contexts within a fixed KV cache budget.
